name: Johan's Library
bio: A running list of books I have read.

books.title: The Buffalo Hunter Hunter
books.author: Stephen Graham Jones
books.notes: I really enjoyed this book, a great vampire story.

books.title: What moves at night
books.author: T. Kingfisher
books.notes: It seems I like everything from T. Kingfisher. This read did not scare me as much as the first book in this series but it was a great read anyway.

books.title: Drive your plow over the bones of the dead
books.author: Olga Tokarczuk
books.notes: I'm not used to Nobel prize winners being so readable, but this novel was very much so. A murder mystery set in a small village in the polish countryside. The main character is a former bridge architect who now works part time as a teacher. The police isn't seeing clearly so the main character does her own digging. Great read!

books.title: The vegetarian
books.author: Han Kang
books.notes: A wife stops eating meat and her husband, parents and siblings cannot accept it. I haven't read much south korean literature but I'm pretty sure this is not the book to define it. This really moved me, a book that you'll not forget, it was dark, brutal and sad.

books.title: Creation Lake
books.author: Rachel Kushner
books.notes: Some books are just easy to read, the pages fly away without you noticing and this is one of those books. The main character Sadie Smith is an under cover instigator, paid by an unknown power. She has hacked the target Bruno Lacombe's email and every other chapter or so is an email, often involving a story or idea about Neanderthals. It's a bit weird but it works really well.

books.title: I Cheerfully Refuse
books.author: Leif Enger
books.notes: I like that we're not spoon fed an explanation for the state of the world, but rather gradually realize that not everything is what it seems.

books.title: What moves the dead
books.author: T. Kingfisher
books.notes: Reading this gave me chills! I read it far too late into the nights but it was a treat!

books.title: The passage
books.author: Justin Cronin
books.notes: I read the collection, 766 pages with a cliffhanger at the end of every chapter. It's a lot writers' tricks in there, everything mentioned comes back. I want to dislike it, but I enjoyed this read even though it had its flaws. The first section is great, present day, ends with an apocalypse, a bit simple but still good characters. Second section, I almost gave up here - I did NOT want to read another Hunger Games. When I saw the map of the camp I just wanted to close the book and read something else. But. But. I bit the bullet and kept on. I liked the characters and their struggles. You knew the camp was going to break, you knew the outseide was going to come in, you knew the characters knew it, you knew it was bound to happen and it was, unfortunately, at the end of the section, a bit rushed. But I kept readong and I thought it came through up until the last section. Where it's all supposed to come together. But. It doesn't really work for some reason. Babcock, is just big, not as interesting in flesh as in the dreams. Considering the difficulties in the start, it's a bit too easy in the end. And then, the actual end, I don't know what to make of it. Was there dices involved? I don't understand the end. But these stories usually lingers for a long time, and that's the good stories. And this was one of them, a good story.

books.title: The familiar
books.author: Leigh Bardugo
books.notes: This was a great read. Born into a near impossible situation the main character Luzia is doomed from the start, she wants to be herself but that's not allowed in Spain in 16th century. There are some historical figures in there (who undoubtedly did some shady stuff) which Leigh Bardugo writes a great story on.

books.title: Graveyard Shift
books.author: M.L. Rio
books.notes: I read What moves at night earlier this year and both novellas involving fungi I could not help comparing them to each other. My impression of this book was that it never started, it was laying the groundwork, introducing the characters, villain, monsters and then... it ended.

books.title: I who have never known men
books.author: Jacqueline Harpman
books.notes: I didn't know what to expect of this book. What intrigued me was that this dystopian novel was overlooked when it was first released in 1995, it didn't sell and was mostly forgotten. Then a publisher rediscovered it and re-released it in 2022 and it became a success. The novel is a story about forty women kept prisoners underground, without knowing why or by whom. The guards does not talk to them at all and the women has mostly accepted their fate. Except for the youngest woman, a rebel not accepting the status quo. I don't want to spoil anything but it was a great read! A story who is allowed to be a story and not serve everything on a platter like some modern tales are told. Refreshing!

books.title: The devils
books.author: Joe Abercrombie
books.notes: This was a blast, very much like The Kings of Wyld by Nicholas Eames. Set in a medieval Europe with a heavy fantasy setting. There is an on-going war between two christian factions and a brother monk is tasked with delivering a package together with a group of blasphemous creatures. Lots of action and fun!

books.title: Propeth song
books.author: Paul Lynch
books.notes: Ireland is falling into tyranny and a mother tries to keep the family together while the father has been disappeared by the ruling party. It just continues downhill and gets worse and worse.

books.title: Vigil
books.author: George Saunders
books.notes: I like reading George Saunders, the language is great as always and just a treat to read. The story in Vigil revoles around a supernatural being named Jill. She is being tasked with comforting the dying greedy fossil fuel company executive. Looking back at his legacy, why isn't there any remorse? The story is full of of wonderful fantasy, but at its core it is a classic story about greed and absolute justice, is there good and evil?

books.title: The Starving Saints
books.author: Caitlin Starling
books.notes: A sieged castle is filled with refugees and the food is running out. We follow three main characters with different goals who are forced to work together when strange things start to happen inside the walls. We ave one valiant knight, a noble that is hiding as a servant, and finally a self thaught witch which doesn't know what she's doing. I really enjoyed this book even though it was a bit gory, great threats and magic.

books.title: Steel Lobsters
books.author: Myke Cole
books.notes: The last knights in England. On horse and in full armor that is. Occasionally I read a history book, and this one is about knights with guns and they were called Steel Lobsters, that's too good to pass up. It deals with the English civil war between Royalists and Parlamentarians. On the parliamentarian side a man named Arthur Hesilrige builds this company of heavy cavalry in a time when the swedish king Gustav Adolf was changing the way wars were fought. So sir Hesilrige had a difficult task ahead of him and the author explains why they failed in the end. If you like knights and/or gunpowder this is a great read.

books.title: Between two fires
books.author: Christopher Buehlman
books.notes: Every time I get a cold or a fever I read a book with either plauge or some other sickness that turns everyone into zombies. This time I picked up Between two fires, which I've been wanting to read ever since I heard about it. It's a story about a knight turned bandit, a lost priest and girl oprhaned by the Black death. You had me at the Black death. I've been fascinated by this apocalypse since I was a kid, and the first real history books I read was Den svarta döden by Dick Harrison. But Between two fires takes place in a plague ridden Europe where magical things happen. It's bleak, bloody and fantastic. Chrisopher Buehlman is a great writer and it's a treat to read every page. I read this book in a couple of nights. It reminded me of 'The Devils' by Joe Abercrombie and 'The Starving Saints' by Caitlin Starling, all great reads. I'll read this again I'm sure.
